Image via Netflix

Another prematurely cancelled series is heading to Netflix this month, where it will surely find a second life. Made as a sequel to a critically acclaimed dramedy, this two-season hit follows a mother whose partner of 12 years and father of their son is suddenly incarcerated. The situation forces her to move in with his mother and half-sister, leaving her to navigate a chaotic, humorous existential crisis.

The comedy series premiered on June 13, 2021, on Starz, earning a perfect Certified Fresh 100% critics rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with the consensus describing it as a “rare adaptation that exceeds its source material.” Later in October 2021, the series was renewed for a second season, which premiered on April 14, 2023, to another 100% Tomatometer score. Despite the stellar reception, the network canceled it in September that year alongside three other Starz shows, with reports saying it "unfortunately did not find a large enough audience" to warrant more episodes.

Created by Daveed Diggs and Rafael Casal, Blindspotting is a sequel to their 2018 film of the same name, set six months later. Fans may remember Diggs for his most recent portrayal of the Supe, Oh Father, in the superhero series The Boys. Oh Father is a corrupt and deeply questionable preacher whom Homelander recruits to play a pivotal role in Vought-American's future. Now, three years after Diggs' show Blindspotting was canceled, all sixteen episodes, eight from Seasons 1 and 2, will launch on Netflix U.S. on October 20, 2026.
